items.title: Dave McKenna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: “No Bass Hit” was the first one with Concord, and that was with Jake and Scott.

ctx.x: Well I like some of your album titles too, they’re creative. You had “No Bass Hit”—

I think that was, I’ve got to give Carl Jefferson credit. I think he came up with that and “Major League.” Those were the two with — “No Bass Hit” was the first one with Concord, and that was with Jake and Scott. And then I did a solo album shortly after, and “Major League” was a few years later, and for Concord I did a trio album playing that Harry Warren music, and I did an album with Gray Sargent, a duo; and an album with Joe Temperley, a duo; an album with Buddy DeFranco, a duo; a lot of duos; plus the things…
You had mentioned that there was a time in your life when you were thinking about the post office.

items.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: And anyway, to work with McKenna, you know, beautiful. Then we added Bob Wilber and Cutty Cutshall and we went out and we always had that good quartet, you know.

ctx.x: Well you eventually went and played with Marian.

Yeah. Well I went into Swing music forever. I never went back to the bebop thing. Never went back to it, I never went back, no. I went out with Marian, right after that I went with her trio, for years. I was in the Hickory House for years with Toshiko you know. I was with Maynard Ferguson at Birdland and things like that. Once I got with these guys, that was it. That was it. I headed for John Bunch and Count Basie, playing with Count in a little combos you know, oh, Dave McKenna, and after Marian I went right…
Well do you know what it was about your playing that they liked?
